summary: Portland International Jetport (PWM) is Maine's largest and busiest airport, located just three miles west of downtown Portland. Established in 1931, it has grown into a modern facility serving over two million passengers annually with nonstop flights to major U.S. hubs. The airport is known for its compact, easy-to-navigate layout and Maine-themed décor, including local art and regional cuisine.
faqs:
Q: What airlines fly out of Portland International Jetport?
A: Major carriers include American Airlines, Delta Air Lines, JetBlue, Southwest Airlines, and United Airlines, offering nonstop service to destinations like New York, Atlanta, Chicago, and Washington, D.C.

Q: How do I get from the airport to downtown Portland?
A: Greater Portland Metro bus route 5 runs between the airport and downtown Portland approximately every 30-60 minutes. Taxis, rideshares (Uber/Lyft), and rental cars are also available on-site.

Q: How far is PWM from downtown Portland?
A: The airport is about 3 miles (5 km) from downtown, typically a 10-15 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: What amenities are available at the airport?
A: Free Wi-Fi, a variety of dining options including local seafood, gift shops, and art installations. There is also a business center and charging stations throughout the terminal.
transport_tips: The airport is easily accessible via I-95 and Congress Street. Greater Portland Metro bus route 5 offers an affordable ride to downtown for $2.00 (exact change required). Taxis and rideshares pick up outside baggage claim, and rental cars are located in the parking garage. For drop-offs and pickups, use the free cell phone lot to avoid congestion.
local_tip: Frequent visitors know the free cell phone lot on Jetport Boulevard has a digital flight status board and is the best place to wait for arriving passengers—it saves circling the terminal and reduces stress.
